paragraphs.title: Moses Sees the Land from Mount Nebo

easy.question: Which mountain did Moses climb?
answers: Mount Nebo
Mount Carmel
Mount Sinai
easy.explanation: The verse says, “And Moses went up ... unto the mountain of Nebo.”

easy.question: Who showed Moses the whole land?
answers: Joshua
The Lord
The children of Israel
easy.explanation: The verse says, “And the Lord shewed him all the land.”

easy.question: As far as which city did the view Moses saw extend?
answers: Dan
Jerusalem
Zoar
easy.explanation: The end of verse 3 says, “unto Zoar.”

medium.question: What happened first in the order of the verses?
answers: The Lord showed Moses the whole land
Moses went up from the plains of Moab to Mount Nebo
Moses saw as far as Zoar
medium.explanation: First Moses went up to Mount Nebo; afterward the Lord showed him the land.

medium.question: In the phrase “the plain of the valley of Jericho,” what kind of place is being described?
answers: A high mountain
A fortified city
A broad, level area
medium.explanation: The verse mentions a plain and a valley, describing a broad, level area.

medium.question: What does the long list of regions show about what the Lord showed Moses?
answers: The view included many large parts of the land
Moses visited every city
Only one region was important
medium.explanation: The verses mention many regions, from Gilead to the south and the plain, emphasizing the wide extent of the land Moses saw.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the fact that Moses saw the land from the top of Pisgah?
answers: He entered every region he saw
He saw only the city of Jericho
The high place allowed him to look over a wide area
challenge.explanation: “The top of Pisgah” describes a high viewpoint suitable for seeing a broad area.

challenge.question: In the context of the land of Judah, what does “unto the utmost sea” indicate?
answers: The land extended westward to the sea
It was the last sea seen in time
It was the name of a city in Judah
challenge.explanation: The phrase appears in a description of the land’s boundaries, indicating the sea as its western limit.

challenge.question: Which precise distinction emerges from the verses?
answers: The verses say that Moses conquered the whole land
The verses describe the land Moses saw, not that he entered it
The verses say that Moses saw only the land east of Jordan
challenge.explanation: The verses say that the Lord showed Moses the land, but do not say that Moses entered or conquered it.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the fact that Moses saw the land from the top of Pisgah?
answers: He entered every region he saw
He saw only the city of Jericho
The high place allowed him to look over a wide area
questions.explanation: “The top of Pisgah” describes a high viewpoint suitable for seeing a broad area.

questions.question: In the context of the land of Judah, what does “unto the utmost sea” indicate?
answers: The land extended westward to the sea
It was the last sea seen in time
It was the name of a city in Judah
questions.explanation: The phrase appears in a description of the land’s boundaries, indicating the sea as its western limit.

questions.question: Which precise distinction emerges from the verses?
answers: The verses say that Moses conquered the whole land
The verses describe the land Moses saw, not that he entered it
The verses say that Moses saw only the land east of Jordan
questions.explanation: The verses say that the Lord showed Moses the land, but do not say that Moses entered or conquered it.

paragraphs.title: The Promise of the Land and the Limit of Moses’ Mission

easy.question: Who spoke to Moses in the verse?
answers: The Lord
Abraham
Joshua
easy.explanation: The verse begins, “And the Lord said unto him,” so the speaker is the Lord.

easy.question: To whom had the Lord sworn that He would give the land to their descendants?
answers: Moses, Aaron, and Joshua
Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob
Noah, Shem, and Ham
easy.explanation: The Lord recalls His oath to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob to give the land to their descendants.

easy.question: What was Moses told about going into the land?
answers: He would enter it immediately
He would enter only with Joshua
He would not go over into it
easy.explanation: The verse says, “but thou shalt not go over thither,” meaning Moses would not enter the land.

medium.question: Why did the Lord show Moses the land?
answers: So Moses could choose the king
Because it was the land promised to the fathers and their descendants
So Moses could build the tabernacle there
medium.explanation: The Lord showed Moses the land He had sworn to give to Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and their descendants.

medium.question: What is the order of events in the verse?
answers: The Lord recalls the oath, shows Moses the land, and then says Moses will not enter it
Moses enters the land, the Lord swears to the fathers, and then the land is given to their descendants
The Lord gives the land to Moses and then swears to the fathers
medium.explanation: The oath to the fathers is mentioned first; then the Lord shows Moses the land and says he will not enter it.

medium.question: In the phrase “I will give it unto thy seed,” who are Moses’ “seed”?
answers: His descendants
His land
His friends
medium.explanation: “Thy seed” means descendants or future generations; the context says the land will be given to them.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the contrast between “I have caused thee to see it with thine eyes” and “thou shalt not go over thither”?
answers: Moses saw the land but did not enter it
Moses entered the land but did not see it
Moses did not see the land at all
challenge.explanation: The verse emphasizes that Moses was allowed to see the land but was not allowed to enter it.

challenge.question: To whom does “thou shalt not go over” refer?
answers: Moses’ descendants
Moses, whom the Lord was addressing
Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob
challenge.explanation: The Lord speaks to Moses in the singular—“thee” and “thou”—so the restriction applies to Moses.

challenge.question: What central idea emerges from the land being given to “thy seed” rather than to Moses himself?
answers: The promise to the fathers is fulfilled through future generations
The land is given only to Moses
The promise to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob was canceled
challenge.explanation: The verse connects the oath to the fathers with giving the land to their descendants, even though Moses himself does not enter it.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the contrast between “I have caused thee to see it with thine eyes” and “thou shalt not go over thither”?
answers: Moses saw the land but did not enter it
Moses entered the land but did not see it
Moses did not see the land at all
questions.explanation: The verse emphasizes that Moses was allowed to see the land but was not allowed to enter it.

questions.question: To whom does “thou shalt not go over” refer?
answers: Moses’ descendants
Moses, whom the Lord was addressing
Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob
questions.explanation: The Lord speaks to Moses in the singular—“thee” and “thou”—so the restriction applies to Moses.

questions.question: What central idea emerges from the land being given to “thy seed” rather than to Moses himself?
answers: The promise to the fathers is fulfilled through future generations
The land is given only to Moses
The promise to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob was canceled
questions.explanation: The verse connects the oath to the fathers with giving the land to their descendants, even though Moses himself does not enter it.

paragraphs.title: The Death and Hidden Burial of Moses

easy.question: Where did Moses die?
answers: In the land of Moab
In the land of Egypt
In the land of Canaan
easy.explanation: The verse says that Moses died in the land of Moab.

easy.question: How old was Moses when he died?
answers: One hundred years old
One hundred and twenty years old
Eighty years old
easy.explanation: The verse says that Moses was one hundred and twenty years old when he died.

easy.question: What does the verse say about Moses’ eye?
answers: It was weak
It was closed
It was not dim
easy.explanation: The verse says, “his eye was not dim.”

medium.question: What was unusual about Moses’ burial?
answers: No one knew where he was buried
He was buried in Egypt
He was buried inside Bethpeor
medium.explanation: The verse says that no man knew the location of his sepulchre to that day.

medium.question: Which detail shows that Moses remained physically strong at age 120?
answers: He was buried in the land of Moab
His eye was not dim, nor his natural force abated
He was opposite Bethpeor
medium.explanation: The verse emphasizes that his sight and natural strength had not weakened even in old age.

medium.question: In the phrase “nor his natural force abated,” what is being described?
answers: He did not travel from place to place
He did not feel thirsty
His strength and vitality had not decreased
medium.explanation: Together with “his eye was not dim,” the phrase says that Moses remained strong and vigorous.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the fact that Moses’ burial place was unknown, even though the region is identified?
answers: He was buried in another land
The verse does not know where he was buried
The place was not turned into a shrine around his grave
challenge.explanation: The verse identifies the general area but emphasizes that no one knew the exact burial place.

challenge.question: What sequence of events is described in the verses?
answers: Moses died, was buried, and his age and condition were described
Moses was buried, was born, and then died
Moses grew old, entered Canaan, and then was buried
challenge.explanation: The passage first describes Moses’ death, then his burial, and finally his age and physical condition.

challenge.question: What is the possible significance of calling Moses “the servant of the Lord” at the time of his death?
answers: Moses was an enslaved person
It describes his faithfulness and service to the Lord
He served only in the land of Moab
challenge.explanation: The title presents Moses as the Lord’s faithful servant, not as someone enslaved to a human master.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the fact that Moses’ burial place was unknown, even though the region is identified?
answers: He was buried in another land
The verse does not know where he was buried
The place was not turned into a shrine around his grave
questions.explanation: The verse identifies the general area but emphasizes that no one knew the exact burial place.

questions.question: What sequence of events is described in the verses?
answers: Moses died, was buried, and his age and condition were described
Moses was buried, was born, and then died
Moses grew old, entered Canaan, and then was buried
questions.explanation: The passage first describes Moses’ death, then his burial, and finally his age and physical condition.

questions.question: What is the possible significance of calling Moses “the servant of the Lord” at the time of his death?
answers: Moses was an enslaved person
It describes his faithfulness and service to the Lord
He served only in the land of Moab
questions.explanation: The title presents Moses as the Lord’s faithful servant, not as someone enslaved to a human master.

easy.question: For whom did the children of Israel weep?
answers: Moses
Aaron
Joshua
easy.explanation: The verse says, “And the children of Israel wept for Moses.”

easy.question: How long did the children of Israel weep?
answers: Seven days
Thirty days
Forty days
easy.explanation: The verse says that they wept for thirty days.

easy.question: Where did the children of Israel mourn for Moses?
answers: In the wilderness of Sinai
In Jerusalem
In the plains of Moab
easy.explanation: The verse identifies the place as the plains of Moab.

medium.question: In the phrase “the days of weeping and mourning for Moses were ended,” what does “ended” mean?
answers: Came to an end
Began
Became longer
medium.explanation: The phrase says that the days of weeping and mourning came to an end.

medium.question: What does the connection between “thirty days” and “the days of weeping and mourning for Moses were ended” show?
answers: The mourning lasted only one day
The mourning lasted thirty days and then ended
The mourning began only after thirty days
medium.explanation: The verse describes thirty days of weeping and mourning, after which the mourning ended.

medium.question: Who were the mourners according to the verse?
answers: Only Moses’ family
Only the elders of Israel
The children of Israel
medium.explanation: The verse describes the children of Israel as those who wept and mourned for Moses.

challenge.question: What conclusion fits the verse’s mention of both weeping and mourning?
answers: The people openly expressed their sorrow for Moses
The people felt no sorrow
The people celebrated Moses’ death
challenge.explanation: Weeping and mourning express sorrow, so the verse emphasizes the people’s public grief for Moses.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the plural expression “the children of Israel”?
answers: Only one person mourned
The mourning included the nation or many of its people
Only Moses himself mourned
challenge.explanation: The plural expression refers to many people, indicating broad public mourning rather than the grief of one person.

challenge.question: What is the correct order of events in the verse?
answers: The mourning ended, and only afterward did the weeping begin
The Israelites moved elsewhere and then wept
The children of Israel wept for thirty days, and then the mourning ended
challenge.explanation: The verse first describes thirty days of weeping and then says that the days of mourning ended.

questions.question: What conclusion fits the verse’s mention of both weeping and mourning?
answers: The people openly expressed their sorrow for Moses
The people felt no sorrow
The people celebrated Moses’ death
questions.explanation: Weeping and mourning express sorrow, so the verse emphasizes the people’s public grief for Moses.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the plural expression “the children of Israel”?
answers: Only one person mourned
The mourning included the nation or many of its people
Only Moses himself mourned
questions.explanation: The plural expression refers to many people, indicating broad public mourning rather than the grief of one person.

questions.question: What is the correct order of events in the verse?
answers: The mourning ended, and only afterward did the weeping begin
The Israelites moved elsewhere and then wept
The children of Israel wept for thirty days, and then the mourning ended
questions.explanation: The verse first describes thirty days of weeping and then says that the days of mourning ended.

easy.question: Who was full of the spirit of wisdom?
answers: Joshua the son of Nun
Moses
The children of Israel
easy.explanation: The verse says, “And Joshua the son of Nun was full of the spirit of wisdom.”

easy.question: What did Moses do to Joshua?
answers: Sent him to Egypt
Laid his hands upon him
Taught him to read
easy.explanation: The verse says that Moses had laid his hands upon Joshua.

easy.question: How did the children of Israel respond to Joshua?
answers: They fled from him
They asked Moses to replace him
They obeyed him and did as the Lord commanded
easy.explanation: The verse says that the children of Israel hearkened unto Joshua and did as the Lord commanded Moses.

medium.question: What connection does the verse make between Moses laying his hands on Joshua and Joshua’s spirit of wisdom?
answers: It connects the laying on of hands with Joshua being full of wisdom
It says the laying on of hands caused Joshua to leave Israel
It says the laying on of hands punished Joshua
medium.explanation: The verse links Moses’ action with Joshua being full of the spirit of wisdom.

medium.question: In the phrase “Moses had laid his hands upon him,” what does “laid” mean?
answers: Abandoned
Placed or put
Called out
medium.explanation: In this context, “laid his hands upon him” means that Moses placed his hands on Joshua.

medium.question: What sequence of events is described in the verse?
answers: Israel commanded Moses, and then Joshua was chosen
Joshua listened to Israel, and then Moses laid his hands on him
Moses laid his hands on Joshua, the people listened to him, and they followed the Lord’s command
medium.explanation: First Moses laid his hands on Joshua; afterward the people listened to him and acted according to the Lord’s command.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the connection between Moses laying his hands on Joshua and Joshua’s spirit of wisdom?
answers: Moses’ action symbolized Joshua’s preparation and succession as leader
Moses wanted to distance Joshua from the people
Joshua became wise only because of his age
challenge.explanation: The verse connects the laying on of hands with Joshua’s wisdom, suggesting his preparation and appointment as leader.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “as the Lord commanded Moses” emphasize about Joshua’s leadership?
answers: Joshua canceled Moses’ words
Joshua’s leadership continued the divine command given to Moses
The Israelites acted only according to their own decisions
challenge.explanation: The phrase shows that the people followed the command the Lord had given Moses, rather than Joshua’s personal wishes alone.

challenge.question: Which detail shows that Joshua was accepted as an actual leader, not merely prepared for leadership?
answers: He was called the son of Nun
Moses laid his hands upon him
The children of Israel listened to him and obeyed
challenge.explanation: The people’s obedience to Joshua shows that his leadership was accepted in practice.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the connection between Moses laying his hands on Joshua and Joshua’s spirit of wisdom?
answers: Moses’ action symbolized Joshua’s preparation and succession as leader
Moses wanted to distance Joshua from the people
Joshua became wise only because of his age
questions.explanation: The verse connects the laying on of hands with Joshua’s wisdom, suggesting his preparation and appointment as leader.

questions.question: What does the phrase “as the Lord commanded Moses” emphasize about Joshua’s leadership?
answers: Joshua canceled Moses’ words

questions.explanation: The phrase shows that the people followed the command the Lord had given Moses, rather than Joshua’s personal wishes alone.

questions.question: Which detail shows that Joshua was accepted as an actual leader, not merely prepared for leadership?
answers: He was called the son of Nun
Moses laid his hands upon him
The children of Israel listened to him and obeyed
questions.explanation: The people’s obedience to Joshua shows that his leadership was accepted in practice.

paragraphs.title: Moses’ Uniqueness and His Miraculous Signs

easy.question: Among whom had no prophet arisen like Moses?
answers: In Israel
In Egypt
In Canaan
easy.explanation: The verse says, “And there arose not a prophet since in Israel like unto Moses.”

easy.question: In which land did Moses perform the signs and wonders?
answers: The land of Canaan
The land of Egypt
The land of Edom
easy.explanation: The signs and wonders were performed in Egypt before Pharaoh, his servants, and all his land.

easy.question: Who saw the mighty hand and the great terror shown by Moses?
answers: Pharaoh alone
Pharaoh’s servants alone
All Israel
easy.explanation: The verse says that Moses showed them “in the sight of all Israel.”

medium.question: Why was Moses considered a prophet without equal according to the verses?
answers: The Lord knew him face to face, and he performed many signs and wonders
He was the first person to enter the land of Israel
He was king over Egypt
medium.explanation: The verses emphasize both Moses’ special relationship with the Lord and his signs, wonders, and mighty deeds.

medium.question: In the phrase “all the great terror,” what is being described?
answers: Great joy
Great fear or awe
A long journey
medium.explanation: “Terror” means great fear or awe; the wording emphasizes the powerful impression made by Moses’ deeds.

medium.question: What order of events is described in the verses concerning Moses’ deeds?
answers: All Israel saw him first, and afterward he was sent to Egypt
He entered the land first, and afterward performed signs in Egypt
The Lord sent him to perform signs in Egypt, and then his deeds before Israel are described
medium.explanation: Verse 11 describes the signs in Egypt, and verse 12 adds the mighty hand and great terror shown before Israel.

challenge.question: What can be learned from the phrase “in Israel” in “there arose not a prophet since in Israel like unto Moses”?
answers: The comparison is with the prophets of Israel
Moses was not connected with Israel
Moses worked only in Egypt
challenge.explanation: The phrase defines the scope of the comparison: no prophet arose in Israel like Moses.

challenge.question: What does “in the sight of all Israel” emphasize at the end of the passage?
answers: The deeds happened secretly
The whole nation witnessed the great deeds
Only the leaders understood them
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that the mighty hand and great terror were seen by all Israel, not only by a few people.

challenge.question: How do the two types of deeds in the verses strengthen the description of Moses’ greatness?
answers: They show that Moses dealt only with Egypt
They show that Moses was both a king and a priest
They present both his work before Egypt and his impact on Israel
challenge.explanation: The verses mention the signs in Egypt and the mighty hand and great terror shown before Israel, displaying Moses’ greatness in both settings.

questions.question: What can be learned from the phrase “in Israel” in “there arose not a prophet since in Israel like unto Moses”?
answers: The comparison is with the prophets of Israel

Moses worked only in Egypt
questions.explanation: The phrase defines the scope of the comparison: no prophet arose in Israel like Moses.
